redFirst.basis: regression task with expectRedFirst false; the Windows failures reproduce only on windows-latest, the new CRLF cases are fixtures simulating the shape on any OS

outcome.technical:
Three reader fixes, reasoned from the CI lines (no Windows run here). (1) _HOUSE_ABORT now ends `[ 	]*$`: a Windows interpreter writes print() to a pipe with CRLF, `$` under re.M stops before 
 and the stray  defeated `[ 	]*$`, so the house-abort FAIL line (AttributeError/TypeError) was never read -> sh1, sh3. (2) _wt_text opens with newline='': universal-newline read turned the CRLF working file (the fixtures' _write uses text mode, so CRLF on Windows; autocrlf pinned false so the HEAD blob is CRLF too) into LF while _head_text keeps the blob as is, so every line differed, difflib gave ONE whole-file hunk covering the implementation, and 'none of its 1 changed hunk(s) lies inside a test definition' -> si1, si4. (3) sr44 was a fixture error, not a reader one: node reads a backslash inside double quotes as an escape on every platform, so the test's NODE_OPTIONS value for a Windows path must double its backslashes; the fixture now does (identity on POSIX); _node_words unchanged. Windows behaviour assumed: text-mode stdout writes 
 (Python io docs, newline=None translation on write); open(...,'w') default writes 
 on Windows; git show returns the blob bytes under core.autocrlf=false; node NODE_OPTIONS parser (node src/node_options.cc ParseNodeOptionsEnvVar) treats backslash in a quoted string as an escape. The first two are inferred from the CI failure text, not observed in a Windows traceback. Files: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py, plugins/audit/tests/test_stamp_verification.py. Selftest: 263/263 passed, exit 0; ruff clean.
